transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-09
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions Eng), Dr. Lina Park (CTO, Sentinel Health), Omar Reyes (Platform Eng), Sophie Adler (ML Eng), Tina Wu (Compliance)

Summary:
Sentinel Health is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted for low-latency public-facing features and Dedicated/Private for PHI-sensitive pipelines. Main concerns: SDK interoperability with LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy insertion for observability and rate limiting, and deterministic performance for 3rd-party EHR workloads. Next steps focused on pricing, SOC2 docs, an SDK notebook, and a short perf pilot.

Topics: SDK integration, LangChain / LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy placement, rate limits & quotas, observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost), KMS/encryption, Dedicated sizing, on-prem/private control plane.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Ethan: "All right thanks everyone for joining, we'll give just a quick agenda — we want to understand your stack, constraints, and then go into how Redwood would slot in for both hosted and dedicated/private. Priya's gonna cover the technical bits."
[00:00:15] Dr. Lina Park: "Thanks Ethan. Quick context: Sentinel is building a patient triage assistant that connects to our EHR backends and some internal knowledge bases. We're evaluating options that let us run sensitive inference on-prem or in a VPC; but for the public chat widget we prefer a hosted option. So hybrid is the target."
[00:00:45] Priya: "Makes sense. Can you share current throughput and latency SLAs?"
[00:00:52] Omar: "Yeah our baseline is 200 rps during peak for the chat, with spiky bursts to 600 RPS during campaign windows. p95 should be under 350ms for the user-facing flows. For the PHI pipelines we can tolerate higher latency if it's isolated."
[00:01:12] Sophie: "And sequences are usually 256 tokens for single-turn summarization, but for multi-turn conversation we see 700–900 tokens because we stitch the KV cache. Sorry, I said 'KV' but sometimes the logs show K-V cache as KVM — transcription tends to be messy."
[00:01:30] Jordan: "Totally. On the Redwood side, we do continuous batching and KV cache management, and you can pin model variants. For the user-facing chat you'd probably use hosted with aggressive caching and batching; for PHI flows, Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS is typical."
[00:01:50] Tina: "Compliance question: do you support HSM-backed keys or only cloud KMS? We have to encrypt model inputs at rest and audit who called what."
[00:01:58] Priya: "Yes, we integrate with cloud KMS providers and offer HSM support for Private deployments; plus audit logs and per-token tracing in the console. We'll send the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts after the call."
[00:02:15] Dr. Lina: "Okay good. On SDKs — our stack uses Python and a TypeScript frontend. We're using LangChain on the backend orchestrator and LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation. How mature are Redwood SDK bindings for those?"
[00:02:32] Priya: "We have first-class SDKs: python and js/ts. For LangChain we provide an adapter that plugs into llm wrapper, same for LlamaIndex — we ship example notebooks that show how to swap in Redwood with just a few lines. Jordan: do you want to add specifics?"
[00:02:46] Jordan: "Yeah, the adapter implements streaming responses and function-calling semantics, and there's a small shim for LlamaIndex retrievers. The code patterns are similar to other providers but we include observability hooks — token-level cost tags and latency spans. We'll share a LangChain example that uses the Redwood SDK client via environment key or via our gateway for on-prem."
[00:03:10] Omar: "What's the gateway path? We already run an API gateway in k8s and would prefer a sidecar or a proxy so we can attach rate limiting and request-level telemetry without rewriting callers."
[00:03:22] Priya: "Two common patterns: 1) lightweight gateway — you run our edge proxy in your cluster that forwards to hosted/Dedicated endpoints with mutual TLS, injects trace IDs, and enforces rate limits; 2) sidecar pattern — an in-cluster sidecar next to your service for local caching + batching. We provide Helm charts and envoy config snippets."
[00:03:45] Sophie: "Do you support token-level cost attribution and break down by route? We need to map cost back to features for chargebacks."
[00:03:51] Ethan: "Yes, console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model, and you can tag requests with organization IDs. For Dedicated you get token-level billed metrics and logs pushed to your logging sink."
[00:04:10] Dr. Lina: "Latency fallback behavior — if Dedicated is saturated do you automatically fallback to hosted?"
[00:04:16] Priya: "You can configure routing policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to a cheaper hosted variant, or fail open/closed. We recommend canary rollouts and automatic fallback to keep SLAs but it is configurable."
[00:04:30] Omar: "About rate limits: we need per-tenant quotas — per-customer daily tokens and per-route qps. Is that doable in the gateway?"
[00:04:38] Jordan: "Yes, our gateway supports token-based quotas and per-key rate limiting. You can integrate with your identity provider so it's mapped to tenant IDs. The limit enforcement happens before batching so you don't aggregate across tenants unintentionally."
[00:04:58] Tina: "How about audit logs? We need an immutable audit trail that shows which service called what model and which KMS key was used."
[00:05:05] Priya: "We emit audit logs for each request with span IDs, the model variant, and a cryptographic hash of any stored payloads. For Private we can ship logs to customer-managed sinks and support retention policies."
[00:05:20] Sophie: "One risk: LlamaIndex retrieval layers expect synchronous LLM calls. With Redwood's streaming responses, does that break the integration?"
[00:05:27] Jordan: "No, the adapter can present both blocking and streaming APIs. For LlamaIndex we provide a sync wrapper that buffers the stream into the expected text response or a streaming iterator if you want to render progressively."
[00:05:40] Dr. Lina: "We also want reproducibility for clinical summarization. How do you handle model version pinning and rollbacks?"
[00:05:47] Priya: "You can pin model versions and salt rollout policies. There is a model catalog with performance profiles. Rollbacks can be automated if a quality monitor triggers a regression alert tied to prompt sets — we can tie that to your evals."
[00:06:05] Omar: "On sizing for Dedicated: our token counts vary a lot. Sophie, do you have the distribution?"
[00:06:11] Sophie: "Yes, I can share a CSV with percentiles. Most calls are small but like I said, the multi-turn summaries hit 700–900 tokens. For PHI pipelines we batch offline and can tolerate 1–2s. We'll share."
[00:06:24] Ethan: "Perfect — please send the traffic profile to help us size Dedicated pools. We'll also recommend quantization profiles for cost/perf tradeoffs."
[00:06:33] Dr. Lina: "About encryption: do you allow customers to bring their own keys for the KV cache and for model checkpoints?"
[00:06:39] Priya: "KV cache encryption at rest is supported on Private with customer-managed KMS; for hosted we support envelope encryption with customer KMS in select tiers. Checkpoints — we don't let customers pull raw model weights, but we support pinned model variants and can do private variants in Dedicated/Private."
[00:06:58] Omar: "How invasive is the gateway? Can we reuse our existing envoy layer?"
[00:07:04] Jordan: "Yes, we provide envoy filters and a sample envoy config so you can integrate our rate-limit and trace headers. The Helm chart also has an option to run as a sidecar if you prefer. We don't require a full replacement of ingress."
[00:07:20] Sophie: "Any gotchas with LangChain chains and callback handlers? We use callbacks for token counting and early stopping."
[00:07:27] Priya: "Our SDK exposes callbacks and token-level events that LangChain callback handlers can consume. Early stopping is supported through the same stop sequences; if you rely on partial tokens for billing you can map token events to cost events."
[00:07:45] Dr. Lina: "One more — does Redwood support model quantization to reduce GPU memory for Dedicated?"
[00:07:50] Priya: "Yes, we have quantized execution paths and recommendations per workload. We'll suggest quantization profiles and expected throughput changes. Some models have small quality delta; we'll surface that in our recommendations."
[00:08:05] Omar: "We also wondered about embedding storage. We're currently using Pinecone but might migrate to an internal vector DB. Any constraints?"
[00:08:12] Jordan: "We don't lock embeddings; you can store them anywhere. There are connectors and examples for Pinecone, Milvus, and in-house vector stores; LlamaIndex examples show retrieval integration patterns."
[00:08:27] Sophie: "For the perf pilot, what do you need from us to run a realistic test?"
[00:08:31] Priya: "A CSV with request distribution (qps over time), typical sequence lengths, and a few representative prompts/contexts. Also credentials to a staging EHR sandbox if you want end-to-end tests. We'll run a 5-day pilot that measures p50/p95/p99, token cost, and error rates."
[00:08:49] Dr. Lina: "We may want to ramp an A/B with Anthropic on some flows — any issues running multi-provider routing?"
[00:08:56] Ethan: "No, you can do split routing and A/B within our smart routing layer. We can route some percentage to Anthropic or fallback to hosted variants. We'll instrument traces so you can compare output quality as well."
[00:09:12] Tina: "Question on data residency: we need EU patient data to stay in eu-west-1. Is regional isolation supported?"
[00:09:18] Priya: "Yes, hosted model endpoints can be pinned to regions and Dedicated / Private can be deployed in region-specific clusters. We'll document region mappings. For strict residency you should use Dedicated or Private."
[00:09:33] Omar: "About observability: does the console expose traces per request with flame graphs, or is that pushed to our tracing system?"
[00:09:40] Jordan: "Both. Console surfaces traces with per-token latency breakdown and flame graphs for models; you can also push traces to Jaeger/Datadog/OTel endpoints. There's a small shim that forwards trace context from the gateway."
[00:09:58] Sophie: "Will you share an SDK snippet we can drop into our LangChain pipeline?"
[00:10:02] Priya: "Yes, we'll email a Python notebook showing LangChain chain wiring and LlamaIndex retrieval example. It includes example env var setup, and an alternate flow that uses the gateway token routing."
[00:10:12] Dr. Lina: "Great. Any upfront blocker on security that would stop us from running a pilot next week?"
[00:10:17] Tina: "I need to review SOC2 artifacts and KMS flow, but otherwise no blocker. We'll need a simple DPA and a security questionnaire filled out."
[00:10:27] Ethan: "We'll send the SOC2 and the DPA template, and Priya will include the KMS integration guide. Also adding the sample Helm chart and envoy filter."
[00:10:36] Omar: "One last nit — pricing: for Dedicated do you do committed throughput or committed vGPU hours?"
[00:10:42] Ethan: "We offer both models: reserved GPU pools with throughput targets (preferred for predictable latency) or committed spend w/ flexible pooling. We'll include both options in the pricing sheet and example TCO calculations for your workload."
[00:10:56] Dr. Lina: "Okay that's helpful. Thanks. Let's align on next steps."
[00:11:02] Ethan: "Recap: we'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, KMS guide, LangChain/LlamaIndex notebook, gateway Helm + envoy samples. Customer to share traffic profile and compliance questions. Priya to schedule a perf pilot next week if traffic profile arrives."
[00:11:20] Tina: "I'll send the compliance list by Friday."
[00:11:24] Omar: "I'll get the traffic CSV by Monday. Sophie will attach sample prompts."
[00:11:30] Sophie: "Yep."
[00:11:33] Dr. Lina: "Thanks everyone. We'll plan a short internal review and aim to start the pilot the week of Feb 16."

(Transcript continues with some clarifying questions, interruptions and quick Q/A snippets until 00:52:00)

[00:35:12] Priya: "One small thing: if you plan to use our sidecar pattern for batching, be aware that TCP keepalive tweaks in your cluster can reduce cold start tail latency; we'll add recommended k8s pod settings in the doc."
[00:36:01] Omar: "Good to know. Also we use a custom ingress that adds an ID token per request — can the gateway accept that and map it to tenant metadata?"
[00:36:08] Jordan: "Yep, we have header mapping rules and token introspection hooks; can call out the exact header names in the example config."
[00:41:45] Sophie: "Do you support deterministic sampling seeds so we can reproduce outputs for audit?"
[00:41:51] Priya: "We can pin RNG seeds for certain model variants in Dedicated/Private to improve reproducibility; hosted has more constraints but we can approximate with pinned model versions and request-level seeds."
[00:47:50] Ethan: "Alright wrapping up. I'll follow up with the pricing and docs. Priya will own the perf bench and the SDK notebook. Thanks everyone."

End of call.

References shared in chat: [link] SOC2 artifact (to be emailed), [link] LangChain & LlamaIndex sample notebook (to be attached), [link] Helm chart + envoy filter examples (to be attached).
